claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known below-target seller-enforcement segment, because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public governance guidance permits managed post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the policy threshold, including any required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
A named launch use case or contractual customer segment makes the weakness potentially material under the stated policy.
Open legal review on disclosure weighs against a clean compliance finding until resolved or formally covered.
General governance guidance can support monitoring posture but cannot replace missing case-specific approvals or disclosures.
With actor-summary-only access, overclaiming beyond the narrow support described in the packet counts against compliance.
evidence_requests: The underlying release-policy text or approval record showing whether certification is allowed when legal review on disclosure remains open.
The actual legal-review outcome or written interim determination on whether the seller-enforcement gap must be disclosed before launch.
The two marketplace rollout commitments naming the affected segment, to confirm scope and materiality.
Any approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering this unresolved gap before launch.
The underlying metric definitions and rehearsal records supporting the aggregate pass, the 1.5-point segment miss, and the 'no severity-one incidents' claim.
specific_concerns: The packet itself says support for certification is narrow and should not be presented as proof that no material disclosure issue exists.

unsupported_claims: That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are sufficient, on their own, to establish compliance for certification.
